slides.title: 19.1.2 Identifying Optimal Substructure
keyPoints: The base value is F(0)=0.

slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 19, treat 19.1.2 Identifying Optimal Substructure as an algorithmic claim. The base value is F(0)=0. For positive a, try every denomination c not exceeding a. When F(a-c) is possible, it gives a candidate F(a-c)+1. The minimum candidate is the answer; no candidate means impossible. To justify optimal substructure, take an optimal nonempty combination and remove one chosen coin c. If its remainder were not optimally solved, replacing that remainder by a better solution would improve the original combination, contradicting optimality. Conversely, every candidate is feasible because it adds a valid coin to a feasible remainder. Positive denominations ensure a-c<a, making the dependency graph acyclic. A zero denomination would recurse into the same unresolved amount, and a negative denomination could increase it. Validation is therefore part of termination and correctness, not only user-interface friendliness. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. Ask what invariant is preserved, what state changes, why termination follows, what input size controls cost, and what output or diagnostic proves the implementation matched the specification.

slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 19, treat Derive a table before reading the implementation as an algorithmic claim. For denominations one, three, and four, fill amounts zero through six by hand. Record zero coins for zero. For each later amount, list the fitting last denominations and the already known predecessor counts. Amount four can use one coin, while amount six compares the predecessor for three against the predecessor for four and chooses two coins through a three. Add a second column containing the chosen last denomination. Follow it backward from six to zero. This makes the difference between computing an optimum value and recovering a witness concrete. Then repeat with denominations two and four and target three. No fitting chain reaches zero, so the result must remain absent rather than becoming a huge sentinel count in the public output. slides.title: Failure clinic — A table hides an invalid state model
keyPoints: A programmer adds a finite stock count to each denomination but leaves the memo key as the remaining amount.

The resulting table can be internally consistent while solving the wrong problem.

Write two concrete paths that reach the same numeric amount with different future options. If they require different answers, they cannot share one cache entry under that key.
